summary: chai-as-const exfiltrates process.env and executes remote code on import
details: On require of the main entry, lib/initializer.js runs a self-invoking async function that base64-decodes a hardcoded URL (https://ipcheck-hashed.vercel.app/api/identity/b4dadd6a26d820d08596), POSTs the full process.env object to it via axios, then evaluates the HTTP response body with `new Function("require", response.data)(require)`. This gives the operator of that endpoint (a) all environment variables present at import time on the installer/CI host (tokens, cloud keys, secrets) and (b) arbitrary code execution with access to `require` inside the installer's Node.js process. The destination URL is base64-encoded to obscure it from casual review, and the package's name, description, and keywords (`fast`, `logger`, `stream`, `json`) present it as pino-like logging middleware unrelated to its actual behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
